speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry requires Uber and GrabCar vehicles to have the same insurance and car inspection schedules as taxis in Singapore; (b) why is the duration of courses for taxi and private hire drivers different; (c) whether there is an age restriction on Uber and GrabCar drivers; and (d) whether permanent residents and work permit holders who possess Singapore driving licences are eligible to be Uber and GrabCar drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Specifically, this means that passengers in a private hire car that is involved in a motor accident can claim compensation from the owner of the private hire car or its insurer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Both taxis and private hire cars are required to procure insurance which covers the use of the vehicles for hire and reward purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This is because the Land Transport Authority (LTA)'s data show that, on average, currently, taxis run about 145,000 km annually, about five times the annual mileage of private hire cars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA will review the data regularly to see if there is a need to adjust the inspection frequency for private hire cars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The difference in training hours is mainly because taxi drivers can pick up street hail jobs, while private hire car drivers are not allowed to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Street hail jobs comprise 80% of all taxi trips, and the additional navigational and route planning components of the taxi driving course train taxi drivers for this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Taxi drivers must also be able to use a taxi meter correctly and be familiar with the various regulations concerning fare collection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, they must have held a driving licence for at least two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The maximum age for private hire car drivers will be 75 years, like for taxi drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Today, traditional limousine companies and car rental companies employ Permanent Residents and Work Pass holders as drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Work Pass holders are subject to Work Pass conditions stipulated by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: They provide chauffeured services that can be chartered for trips like airport transfers and ferrying of VIPs at events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In order to not disrupt traditional limousine companies and car rental companies when the new regulatory regime is implemented, these Permanent Residents and Work Pass holders will also be able to apply for the Private Hire Car Driver Vocational Licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, Permanent Residents and Work Pass holders can only provide chauffeured services in the course of their employment under these car rental or limousine companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This is unlike for Singaporeans, who can be Uber or GrabCar drivers as long as they are sole proprietors of a chauffeured services company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As we understand it, there are no Work Pass holders driving for Uber or Grab today.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have residents who are taxi drivers and their feedback is that they hope to see a more level playing field.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: To get the vocational driving licence, they have a certain minimum number of hours that they need to drive and clock in.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They think that with these Uber and GrabCar drivers, the playing field is not level.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If not, why should we have them in Singapore and create so much unhappiness amongst the taxi drivers?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For the safety of commuters, why can we not specify that there is a minimum age for Uber drivers?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: With regard to a level-playing field, I will break down the answer into two components.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: First of all, in terms of the licensing requirements and so on, it is in accordance with the current practice.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In terms of the need for a Taxi Vocational Licence or a Private Hire Car Driver's Licence (PDVL), there are different conditions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We follow industry practices as best as possible.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When it comes to the impact on taxi drivers and commuters, these were the stipulated principles of how we address the private-hire car industry.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For most, it is commuters' interest; thereafter, the welfare of taxi drivers and private hire car drivers; and the third principle was to allow a transition for the companies, given this disruptive technology in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If we really want to level the field completely, there are two major issues that may not bear the outcomes that we desire.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If you completely level the playing field, it means that the private hire cars will have street hail privileges as well.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This will not bring necessarily the outcomes desired, if it is a complete level playing field.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, in terms of welfare, transition for the taxi drivers, impact on income, we do not want these to be disrupted overnight.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For commuters' interest, if you completely level the playing field and chauffeured service companies and taxi companies become homogenous, then, we will not be able to have the innovative disruption that private hire cars bring to the industry.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the morning peak hours, when we have an inadequate supply of taxi drivers, the commuters' interests are served because there is a supplementary group of drivers that come in the form of Uber and Grab.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As to the age limit of taxi drivers being set at 30, it was for a different set of reasons.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We are open to reviewing this if the taxi industry is requesting for minimum age requirements instead.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A follow-up question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Taking a step back, is it better that we have three categories of drivers, keeping the traditional limo drivers as a separate licence group, the taxi drivers as the first original group and then create a licence group for the private hire 	Page: 13 drivers from Uber and Grab?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Right now, to simplify matters, we have added the traditional limo group into the Uber and Grab group and, therefore, you would require even the traditional group that had been driving without this requirement and new creation, to comply with all the rules.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I thought the Ministry could take one step back and see that there are three categories of licences, so that the rules for Uber and Grab drivers become specific to their requirements and vocation, rather than have them mixed up.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Breaking them up into different parts would mean limo drivers versus private hire car drivers; you will have too many categories.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Many of the limo drivers that I meet at our discussions are also part-time Uber or Grab drivers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Like how we designed the Taxi Driver Vocational Licence versus the PDVL, we allow cross-licensing.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This is part of the review to make it not too cumbersome with too many regulations and for the drivers to not need to jump through too many hoops.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We have not implemented the licensing regime and done a post implementation review.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we will take your views into consideration.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I just have a clarification regarding the answer on the status of persons allowed to drive an Uber or GrabCar.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If they work in a company, which does not exist today, that is a possibility.
